statement: For a connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive graph G, the Benjamini-Schramm conjecture says p_c(G)<p_u(G) iff G is nonamenable.
assumptions: Bernoulli bond percolation; connected locally finite quasi-transitive G; p_c and p_u are the usual existence and uniqueness thresholds.
source: Hutchcroft, Percolation on Hyperbolic Graphs, Conjecture 1.1, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00039-019-00498-0 ; source quote: 'Let G be a connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive graph. Then p_c(G)<p_u(G) if and only if G is nonamenable.'
proof_or_counterexample: Source verification only; this is a conjecture, not an asserted proof.
remaining_gap: Prove nonamenable implies p_c<p_u without an extra structural hypothesis for every Cayley graph.

statement: A connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, nonamenable, Gromov hyperbolic graph satisfies p_c(G)<p_{q->q}(G) for every q in (1,infinity), hence p_c(G)<p_u(G).
assumptions: Bernoulli bond percolation; connected locally finite quasi-transitive nonamenable Gromov hyperbolic G.
source: Hutchcroft, Percolation on Hyperbolic Graphs, Theorem 2.1 and preceding threshold inequality, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00039-019-00498-0 ; source quote: 'Let G be a connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, nonamenable, Gromov hyperbolic graph. Then p_c(G)<p_{q->q}(G) for every q in (1,infinity).'
proof_or_counterexample: Published theorem; the inequality p_{q->q}<=p_u is given immediately before Theorem 2.1.
remaining_gap: A general nonamenable Cayley graph need not satisfy the theorem's Gromov hyperbolicity hypothesis; source does not establish the universal conjecture.

statement: The original 1996 Conjecture 6 asserts p_c(G)<p_u(G) for connected almost transitive G with positive Cheeger constant, in the paper's site-percolation convention; authors say the nonplanar questions extend to bond percolation with minor changes.
assumptions: Connected locally finite almost transitive graph, positive Cheeger constant; independent Bernoulli site percolation in original paper.
source: Benjamini and Schramm (1996), Conjecture 6 and section 2 convention, https://www.maths.tcd.ie/EMIS/journals/EJP-ECP/article/download/978/978-3321-1-PB.pdf ; quote: 'Assume that the almost transitive graph G has positive Cheeger constant. Then pc(G) <pu(G).'
proof_or_counterexample: Direct quotation and scope correction, not a proof.
remaining_gap: For this lane, prove the bond version on every fixed nonamenable Cayley graph.

statement: The OpenAI/math comparator file is not a completed Lean proof of the Benjamini-Schramm nonuniqueness conjecture: the named full_main, critical_laws and cayley_main declarations each end with sorry.
assumptions: Public main-branch file inspected 2026-10-10; no assertion about other files or later revisions.
source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/math/main/lean/ComparatorChallenges/BenjaminiSchramm.lean lines 197-216; source quote: 'theorem full_main ... := by sorry' and likewise critical_laws and cayley_main.
proof_or_counterexample: Inspection of the exact declarations and proof bodies. A sorry admits the proposition without proof and cannot count as a formal check.
remaining_gap: The public preprint's mathematics still needs direct checking; these placeholders alone do not refute the preprint.

statement: For bond percolation on an infinite countable vertex-transitive graph of bounded degree with adjacency norm a>0, if ||T_{p_c}||_{2->2}=M<infinity and p_c<1, then p_c<p_{2->2}<=p_u; specifically ||T_q||<=M/[1-aM(q-p_c)] for p_c<=q<min(1,p_c+1/(aM)).
assumptions: Independent Bernoulli bond law; infinite countable vertex-transitive graph; bounded degree; p_c<1; finite critical two-point operator norm M.
source: w561 ATTEMPT.md L02-L03, independently rederived in w563 VERDICTS.jsonl; owner-own-work; analogous published continuation in the September 2026 manuscript Lemma 2.12.
proof_or_counterexample: Finite-volume Russo pivotal expansion and BK give T'_p<=T_p A T_p entrywise; norm comparison and scalar integration give the displayed bound, with exhaustion to infinity. FKG plus uniqueness would give tau_p(x,y)>=theta(p)^2, contradicting bounded T_p on the infinite graph.
remaining_gap: The premise ||T_{p_c}||<infinity for every fixed nonamenable Cayley graph remains unverified here; the September 2026 manuscript claims it, but its load-bearing proof is not audited.

statement: For a d-regular Cayley graph and normalized simple-random-walk spectral radius rho, the cited Benjamini-Schramm sufficient condition is d*rho*p_c<1. The older stored route using p_c<1/rho omits d and is vacuous whenever 0<rho<1.
assumptions: Infinite connected d-regular Cayley graph; rho=||A||/d in (0,1); Bernoulli bond version of the spectral criterion.
source: Benjamini and Schramm 1996 Theorem 4, https://www.maths.tcd.ie/EMIS/journals/EJP-ECP/article/download/978/978-3321-1-PB.pdf ; w562 S1.w562.002 and w561 L04-L05, independently checked in VERDICTS.jsonl.
proof_or_counterexample: Theorem 4 explicitly requires rho*k*p<1 with k=d. As p_c<=1<1/rho, the degree-free inequality is automatic. T4 has p_c=1/3 and rho=sqrt(3)/2, giving d*rho*p_c=2sqrt(3)/3>1 while p_c<p_u.
remaining_gap: Correcting this sufficient criterion does not establish it for every nonamenable Cayley graph; T4 shows that is not a valid universal strategy.
